about: Agents beyond the twelve this plugin reads directly. usageType says how each reports usage; `unsure` flags a claim that could not be fully verified (with why). Researched 2026-11-22 from the linked sources.

session_weekly.label: Session and weekly limits
session_weekly.tabNote: Has rolling session and weekly limits.

monthly_credits.label: Monthly credits
monthly_credits.tabNote: Usage comes out of a monthly credit allowance.

request_count.label: Request count
request_count.tabNote: Limited by a number of requests per day.

byok_no_limits.label: Bring your own key
byok_no_limits.tabNote: Bring your own key: it adds no limit of its own, so nothing to show here. Any cap is your provider's.

no_usage_data.label: No usage data
no_usage_data.tabNote: Has usage limits but publishes no way to read them, so none are shown.

agents.name: Cline
agents.note: Free; you pay your model provider directly and set your own limits there. Optional ClinePass ($9.99/mo, curated open models) adds 5-hour, weekly and monthly limits. A few Cline-provided models are free in the CLI.
agents.unsure: Mixed: BYOK is the default, but ClinePass has real 5-hour/weekly/monthly windows. A ClinePass user would be session_weekly.

agents.name: Goose
agents.note: Free and open source (Apache 2.0). You pay your model provider's rates; goose has no built-in budget or cap. A local model has no limits at all.

agents.name: Qwen Code
agents.note: The free Qwen OAuth tier was cut to 100 requests/day on 2026-04-13 and discontinued on 2026-04-15. Now it runs on an API key or an Alibaba Coding Plan; Omarchy notes no way to read that plan's quota.
agents.unsure: No official Alibaba pricing page was reachable. Older posts still cite 2,000 requests/day, which is out of date. Coding Plan limits are unverified.

agents.name: Crush
agents.note: Free software; you pay whichever provider you configure (API key, subscription or local model). Charm's own Hyper provider is optional and subscription-based.
agents.unsure: Charm Hyper's free tier and limits are not published in anything reachable; only the provider side is capped.

agents.name: Kilo CLI
agents.note: Free CLI. Model use draws on a prepaid Kilo credit balance shared across Kilo products (inference at provider rates, no markup); Kilo Pass adds monthly credits. This plugin never shows purchasable balances.
agents.unsure: Credits are prepaid and expire, not strictly monthly; Kilo Pass prices came from a third-party summary. It is also BYOK-capable.

agents.name: OpenHands
agents.note: The CLI is free and open source; you pay your LLM provider. OpenHands Cloud sells at-cost credits (new users get $20) and has its own daily-conversation cap on the free individual tier.
agents.unsure: Cloud plan details (Pro price, the 10-conversations/day cap) came from third-party listings. Cloud users would be credit-based.

agents.name: Plandex
agents.note: Free and open source (MIT), self-hosted or local, with your own provider keys (OpenRouter, OpenAI-compatible, Ollama). Plandex Cloud has shut down.

agents.name: CodeWhale
agents.note: A DeepSeek-first terminal agent (formerly DeepSeek TUI). You supply an API key, normally DeepSeek's prepaid balance; it adds no limits of its own.
agents.unsure: Only the project's own README was found, with no pricing or limits statement. The DeepSeek balance model is assumed from its default provider.

agents.name: Reasonix
agents.note: A DeepSeek-focused terminal agent (MIT) built around prefix caching. You supply a DeepSeek API key and pay per token from your balance; it adds no limit of its own.
agents.unsure: Sources disagree on its implementation language and no pricing page exists beyond DeepSeek's own API terms.

agents.name: Aider
agents.note: Free and open source (Apache 2.0). You pay API tokens at your provider's rates; any limits are your provider's. /tokens reports context size and cost in-session. A local Ollama model costs nothing.
agents.unsure: aider.chat itself was not reached; the facts come from guides. The format of /tokens was not verified.

agents.name: Gemini CLI
agents.note: Signing in with a Google account is free for 60 requests/minute and 1,000 requests/day; Google AI Pro raises it to 1,500/day and Ultra to 2,000/day. An agent step can use several requests. A Gemini API key gets 250/day (Flash only).
agents.unsure: One docs mirror listed only the daily cap and another a different tier layout; these figures are the most consistent ones but may have changed.

agents.name: Mistral Vibe
agents.note: Included with Le Chat Pro ($14.99/mo) and Team, with pay-as-you-go beyond the plan budget, or your own API key. Mistral publishes no numeric usage limits (Omarchy's own notes say the same).

agents.name: Factory Droid
agents.note: Plans (Pro $20, Plus $100, Max $200) use independent rolling limits over 5-hour, 7-day and 30-day windows. Factory does not publish the limits in tokens or dollars; /limits in Droid shows your use.
agents.unsure: The pricing page still shows an older Standard Tokens table that conflicts with the rolling-window description; the windows are from the newer text.

agents.name: Augment (Auggie)
agents.note: Standard ($20) and Business ($100) plans include a monthly usage allowance across the model, context engine and compute, which expires at month end. CLI use draws on it; budgets can pause access until next month.
agents.unsure: Augment's docs describe both credits and token-based billing and its plans changed more than once; the exact unit may be dollars of usage, not credits.

agents.name: Pi
agents.note: A free coding harness. Sign in with a subscription you already have (Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot) or use any provider's API key; pi adds no limit of its own.

agents.name: Oh My Pi
agents.note: A free fork of Pi with LSP, subagents and hash-anchored edits. Same model: sign in with /login or use a provider's API key; it adds no limit of its own.

agents.name: DeepSeek Harness
agents.note: DeepSeek's open agent harness (developer preview). You pay DeepSeek per token from a prepaid balance (HTTP 402 at zero); the harness adds no limit of its own. This plugin never shows purchasable balances.
agents.unsure: Developer preview, and the name dsh is also used by community CLIs. The granted-credit expiry window is not published.

agents.name: MiniMax Code
agents.note: Plans have a 5-hour window and a 7-day window (video models only the weekly one), both starting at first use and resetting independently. /status in mcode or `mmx quota` shows usage; exact counts per tier aren't published.

agents.name: Command Code
agents.note: Credit-based: a small monthly plan plus pay-as-you-go top-ups (purchased credits roll over), with new users getting $10 free. Request limits reset each billing cycle; usage is on the Studio billing page.
agents.unsure: Plan prices conflict between the official page ($1/mo Go) and a third-party article ($10/mo), and per-model credit amounts were not found.

agents.name: OpenClaw
agents.note: A gateway agent that reuses your provider keys or subscriptions (Codex, Claude CLI, Coding Plans); it has no limits of its own. `openclaw status --usage` shows your providers' quota windows.
agents.unsure: Whether reusing a Claude subscription is allowed is described as unsettled; check Anthropic's terms. Docs mirrors span several versions.
